name: Ground Items
description:
Things lying on the floor, and what happens when you walk over them. A dungeon's loot used to fall only out of monsters: the chests the stamps laid were drawn and never opened, and there was no way to leave a sword in a room for a player to find. This owns the floor's items. When a floor is generated it reads world.room_template's gear sockets and lays one piece of equipment on each, chosen from a pool by the floor's seed so the same floor offers the same finds; when the player's unit steps onto one, the item is granted through inventory.itemGranted and leaves the floor — unless the bag refuses it, in which case it stays where it was. A reward socket is a chest: stepping onto it opens it once, announced as inventory.containerOpened with the kind 'chest', and inventory.loot_table decides what was inside exactly as it decides what a rock yields. It remembers what was taken and what was opened per floor, so coming back up does not restock the vault.

It draws the items where they lie, through the painter, so a sword on a lattice is on its diamond. It does not draw the chest — the stamp that laid it does — but it publishes which are open so the stamp can draw the lid up. It does not decide what a chest holds, whether an item fits, or what wearing it does: those are the loot table's, the bag's and combat.equipment_slots'.

AND WHAT IS DROPPED. inventory.itemDropped from the panel lays the thing at the tile it names — the player's — or the nearest free tile beside it, where the next footstep can take it back.

AND IT SAYS WHAT IS THERE. Anything lit and within `labelRadius` wears its name on a plate over the tile, drawn at the far end of the depth pass so the wall it lies beside never covers the label. Separately, the moment the light first reaches a thing on this floor it announces inventory.itemSighted — once per thing per floor, and only where a world.vision_system exists to have a moment: a build that sees the whole floor at once has no find to report and reports none. What that becomes in words is ui.event_log's business, not this component's.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: gearPool
inputs.description: Item ids that may lie on a gear socket, drawn by the floor's seed. What each one does when worn is combat.equipment_slots' `gear` map; this only puts them on the floor.

inputs.name: chestKind
inputs.description: The `kind` a reward socket announces itself as when opened, which is the key inventory.loot_table answers under.

inputs.name: pickupOnStep
inputs.description: Whether stepping onto an item takes it. Off, items lie there and a host has to grant them some other way — for a build that wants a pick-up gesture.

inputs.name: minPerFloor
inputs.description: The floor lays at least this many pieces of gear, placing the extras on a floor tile of a room that has none — never the entrance, the stair or the boss's arena. Zero leaves it to the stamps' sockets alone. A run that prices its boss against the gear should not depend on which stamps the rooms happened to roll.

inputs.name: alwaysLay
inputs.description: Items every floor gets one of, laid on a floor tile of a room with nothing in it, whatever the stamps rolled — a key when a door is locked, a potion when the boss hits for five. Laid after the gear sockets and counted apart from minPerFloor.

inputs.name: labelRadius
inputs.description: How near a lying thing names itself, in tiles. A sprite at sixteen pixels on a flagstone is a shape, not a name, and every crawler that puts things on the floor names the one you are walking toward. Two tiles is the reach of a glance; zero turns the names off for a build that wants the picture and nothing else. Only lit things are named, where there is a fog to ask.

outputs.name: items
outputs.description: What lies on the current floor, as {x, y, item}.

outputs.name: itemAt
outputs.description: The item on a tile, or null.

outputs.name: openedAt
outputs.description: Whether the chest on a tile has been opened, so the stamp that drew it can draw it open.

provenance: Asked for by the Dungeon Crawler's first level pass (2026-09-11), with combat.room_encounters: the brief was gear you collect through the area so you are strong enough for the boss, and chests you can actually open. Searched the catalogue first: inventory.loot_table answers what drops and inventory.slotted_bag whether it fits, but nothing put an item on a tile or heard a footstep land on one. Library-native, written against the studio's room stamps, walker and painter.
